question: How many patients with a normal RF don't have thrombosis?
evidence: normal RF refers to RF < 20; don't have thrombosis refers to Thrombosis = '0';
clarification: Count every row, including repeated ID values.
gold: SELECT COUNT(T1.ID) FROM Examination AS T1 INNER JOIN Laboratory AS T2 ON T1.ID = T2.ID WHERE T2.RF < 20 AND T1.Thrombosis = 0
gold0: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT T1.ID) FROM Examination AS T1 INNER JOIN Laboratory AS T2 ON T1.ID = T2.ID WHERE T2.RF < 20 AND T1.Thrombosis = 0

c.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Patient AS p JOIN Laboratory AS l ON p.ID = l.ID JOIN Examination AS e ON p.ID = e.ID WHERE CAST(l.RF AS REAL) < 20 AND e.Thrombosis = 0;

d.request: How many rows have RF < 20 and Thrombosis = '0', counting every row even when ID values repeat?
d.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Laboratory AS l JOIN Examination AS e ON l.ID = e.ID WHERE CAST(l.RF AS REAL) < 20 AND e.Thrombosis = 0;

b.request: Count the rows for which RF is below 20 and Thrombosis equals 0, counting repeated patient IDs separately
b.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Laboratory AS l JOIN Examination AS e ON l.ID = e.ID WHERE CAST(l.RF AS REAL) < 20 AND e.Thrombosis = 0
